root_cause_label: False premise about Whisper GPU dependencies triggers abandonment of the correct tool, followed by a prolonged idle loop imagining ongoing downloads; the agent eventually recovers and produces transcription but the run ends without returning task_complete:true to the grader
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent incorrectly abandoned a working Whisper installation over an imagined GPU-dependency problem, wasted roughly 15 steps in a phantom-download idle loop, eventually transcribed the mislabeled M4A audio with PocketSphinx, but failed to emit the required task_complete confirmation at the final step.
t_err_evidence: Step 5: agent issues 'C-c' as a shell command, claiming CUDA/GPU packages are being downloaded and the installation must be aborted; 'C-c' is not a valid terminal command, the interrupt has no effect, and Whisper can in fact run on CPU — the abandonment rests entirely on an unverified false premise.
t_commit_evidence: Step 40: the grader terminal asks 'Are you sure you want to mark the task as complete? include task_complete:true in your JSON response again' but the trajectory ends without the agent responding; the confirmation is never sent and the benchmark records FAIL.
t_surface_evidence: Step 40 terminal output: 'Are you sure you want to mark the task as complete? This will trigger your solution to be graded and you won't be able to make any further corrections. If so, include "task_complete": true in your JSON response again.' — the explicit failure signal appears at the very last step.
trigger_explanation: At step 5 the agent acts on the unverified belief that pip was downloading large CUDA/GPU libraries incompatible with a CPU-only environment, so it issues 'C-c' to abort Whisper. In fact no CUDA packages were shown in the output (only openai-whisper build deps), Whisper is CPU-compatible, and the 'C-c' text has no effect in the shell interface. This false premise causes the agent to abandon the correct solution path and enter a prolonged multi-tool detour.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5: '(command not found in terminal output)' — the C-c interrupt silently fails, a signal the agent ignores. Steps 8-9: wget and curl both return 'command not found', indicating the download approach is blocked. Steps 11-19: repeated '(command not found in terminal output)' during supposed download waits, meaning the Python one-liners exited immediately yet the agent repeatedly assumes a background download is in progress.
